chats.answer:
For traveling with a laptop and phone, I'd recommend a minimal USB-C charging setup that can handle both devices simultaneously without carrying separate chargers.

My recommended travel charging kit

1. 100W GaN charger

One compact wall charger with 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A port. Look for USB-C PD and enough power to charge your laptop and phone together.

2. Two USB-C cables

A 6 ft (2 m) 240W-rated cable for your laptop and a 3 ft (1 m) cable for your phone. Choose durable braided cables.

3. Optional 20,000 mAh power bank

Choose one with at least 65W USB-C output if you want to charge your laptop away from outlets. Keep it in your carry-on when flying.

4. International travel adapter (if needed)

A compact plug adapter for overseas outlets. Make sure your charger supports 100–240V input.

A 100W charger is a good starting point for most ultrabooks and phones, but a high-performance laptop may require 140W or more.

Anker Prime Charger (100W, 3 Ports, GaN)

One important detail: multiport chargers share power between devices. A 100W charger may provide approximately 65W to a laptop and 30W to a phone when both are connected, depending on the model.

Choose one with at least 65W USB-C output if you want to charge your laptop away from an outlet. Check airline battery limits before flying.

Useful for overseas trips. Make sure the charger supports 100–240V input; a plug adapter does not convert voltage.
